title: Unauthenticated remote code execution in DragonflyDB (memcached reply-builder heap overflow)
summary:
## Summary

When Dragonfly speaks the memcached text protocol, an unauthenticated `get` of an oversized key overflows the 8192 byte reply buffer in `SinkReplyBuilder::WritePieces` and poisons the `next` pointer of an adjacent mimalloc free block (plaintext, `MI_SECURE=0`), so a later allocation is returned at an attacker-chosen fixed address `T`. A second `get` of a big key makes `storage = make_unique<char[]>` land on that block, giving a byte-unrestricted write over the writable GOT. The image sets `__isoc99_sscanf@got` to `base::sh_exec`, and a RESP `RESTORE` of an old string-double sorted set drives `FetchDouble` into `sscanf(score)` == `sh_exec(score)`, running the score string as a shell command. Proven end to end on the stock `ghcr.io/dragonflydb/dragonfly:v1.40.1` image, ASLR on, no information leak, running as the `dfly` service account.

## Severity

Critical, CVSS 3.1 base 9.8 (`AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`). The one precondition is that the operator enabled the memcached protocol (`--memcached_port`, off by default); once enabled it has no authentication at all.

## Root cause

Three pieces of the memcached reply path combine into the overflow.

1. **The reply buffer is hard capped, the copy is not.** In `src/facade/reply_builder.cc`, `SinkReplyBuilder::WritePieces` calls `Flush(required)`, but `Flush` clamps the buffer to `kMaxBufferSize = 8192`, and `write_piece` is a bare `memcpy` with no destination bound.

```cpp
if (size_t required = (piece_size(pieces) + ...); buffer_.AppendLen() <= required)
  Flush(required);                       // buffer capped at kMaxBufferSize = 8192
char* ptr = dest;
([&]() { ptr = write_piece(pieces, ptr); }(), ...);   // unbounded memcpy per piece
```

2. **The unbounded piece is the echoed key.** `MCReplyBuilder::SendValue` builds `WritePieces("VALUE ", key, " ", mc_flag, " ", value.size())`. `"VALUE "` is 6 bytes, so a key of `8192 - 6 + N` bytes writes `N` attacker bytes past the 8192 byte block.

3. **The read path skips every guard.** RESP call sites hand any string over `kMaxInlineSize` (32) to the zero-copy `WriteRef`, and the memcached store and meta paths enforce the 250 byte key limit, but `ParseValueless` in `src/facade/memcache_parser.cc` (serving `get`/`gets`/`gat`/`delete`/`incr`/`decr`) applies neither, so an over long `get` key reaches the unbounded copy intact.

## Why it escalates

The shipped binary is non-PIE, GOT writable (no `BIND_NOW`), no stack canary, and the bundled mimalloc has `MI_SECURE=0` (plaintext free-list `next`). Overflowing reply block `n` overwrites the free neighbour's `next` with `T`. Grooming: open N memcached connections (one reply buffer each), close every other one. A later 8192-class `make_unique<char[]>` (the `storage` for a big `get`) pops `T` and copies attacker bytes there, unrestricted.

## Exploitation

`T = 0x19ef560` is placed 8 bytes above `memcpy@got` (`0x19ef558`), so the `make_unique` zeroing (`memset@got`, `memcpy@got`, both below `T`) never blanks the slots the copy itself needs. The image overwrites `__isoc99_sscanf@got` (`0x19ef658`, above `T`) with `base::sh_exec` (`0x004be2e0`):

```
land      -> make_unique<char[]> pops T = 0x19ef560   (poisoned free-list next)
image     -> sscanf@got (0x19ef658) := base::sh_exec (0x004be2e0)
trigger   -> RESTORE zset(type 3) -> FetchDouble -> sscanf(score) == sh_exec(score)
```

The window image is a faithful copy of the GOT tail with every slot re-armed to its PLT stub (lazy binding re-resolves, process keeps serving), only `sscanf@got` changed plus three ASLR-dependent `.data` pointers neutralized to a fixed readable address. It is precomputed offline from the public binary, so the target's memory is never read: ASLR stays on, no leak. The command uses `bash -c` because `sh_exec` spawns `/bin/sh` (dash), which has no `/dev/tcp`, and is not backgrounded, so the shard thread blocks inside `sh_exec` for the session.
